sections: 19. Estimated WOZ Value - Example - Jan Provostlaan 16, Bilthoven

blocks.text: 17. Estimated WOZ Value - Process

This part describes how the Estimated WOZ Value is calculated for the buildings in table material_estimation_final, the assumptions behind it, and one worked example. WOZ (Waardering Onroerende Zaken - valuation of real estate) is the Dutch property value used for local taxes.
[IMPORTANT] Model estimate, not an official WOZ value. Official WOZ values are set by municipalities; this estimate is not issued by or taken from a municipality, Kadaster or the Waarderingskamer.

Estimated WOZ Value = GO (gebruiksoppervlakte - usable floor area) x base EUR/m2 x type factor x age factor, rounded to the nearest € 1,000. All buildings use the same reference year: WOZ year 2026, valuation date (waardepeildatum) 2025-01-01.
17.1 Step 1 - Find the gemeente (municipality)
PDOK Locatieserver (location server): the postal code (postcode) of the building gives its current gemeentecode (municipality code).
If that fails: the first 4 digits of pand_id (building ID), which are the BAG gemeentecode (municipality code), if CBS still has that gemeente (municipality).
If both fail: the national CBS average (NL01 - the Netherlands).
The municipality column is not used: it comes from the notice text and holds village names and notice fragments that cannot be matched to CBS.
17.2 Step 2 - Base price per m2
Base EUR/m2 = CBS average WOZ value of dwellings (woningen) in the gemeente (municipality) / CBS average floor area of dwellings in the gemeente (municipality).

blocks.text: 17.3 Step 3 - Building type factor
The factor of the BAG gebruiksdoel (use of the building). A building with several uses gets the mean of their factors, each use counted once.
17.4 Step 4 - Age factor
The factor of the band that contains the bouwjaar (year built).
17.5 Step 5 - Floor area and final value
EUR/m2 of the building = base EUR/m2 x type factor x age factor. The estimate is the GO (gebruiksoppervlakte - usable floor area from BAG, go_m2) x EUR/m2 of the building, rounded.
